title: 20 November
subtitle: A special day in BAPS history
headline: BAPS Campus Fellowship Celebrates Diwali, North America
story:
With inspiration from His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj and His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, the BAPS Campus Fellowship has served as a voice of Hinduism and provided genuine care for college youth since the early 2000s. Today, the Fellowship is active at more than 50 campuses across North America.

During November, youths across North American university campuses rekindled their commitment to unity, positivity and spirituality through this year's annual BAPS Campus Diwali Exhibition – In the Joy of Others. With the theme of "Fostering Harmony through Humility," the program focused on the paramount virtue of humility as a pillar of strength, confidence, and success.

The exhibition focused on the need to embrace humility to become leaders of tomorrow and foster harmony in our homes, colleges, and workplaces. Delegates walked away with inspiration to imbibe the paramount quality of humility in their lives: - Diwali is a time to reflect and commit to changing our mindset and perspectives, and take a step forward to becoming better versions of ourselves - Happiness and fulfillment come from harmony (togetherness and inclusiveness) - Harmony is fostered imbibing the value of humility (appreciating others, selfless service, letting go of "need for praise," removing envy, detaching from "end result") - Humility can be imbibed by adopting a positive mindset and deep reflection of "what triggers our negative thoughts." - Becoming humble can allow us to experience fulfillment and happiness at home, personal relationships, career and school - Practice daily mind cleanse to (express gratitude, appreciate others, imbibe good virtues of others in our lives, help because you can and want to, remove the expectation of any return) - Source inspiration from world leaders like His Holiness Pramukh Swãmi Maharaj and His Holiness Mahant Swãmi Maharaj who are beacons of humility and harmony.

The "Festival of Lights" was celebrated in its truest purpose in the context of self-reflection, selfless service, humility, and inspiration of cultivating these qualities within oneself. The Exhibition also showcased exemplary global role models who have made a significant impact in today's world through a humble attitude and approach.

Delegates were inspired by the timely and honest conversation on imbibing the value of humility in order for us to experience the true happiness of Diwali, a reflective time of year.

options.headline: Diwali at the California State Capitol, Sacramento, CA, USA
options.story:
On Monday, November 20, 2023, members of the California State Senate and Assembly and prominent members of the Hindu & Indian American communities gathered to celebrate the festival of Diwali at the California State Capitol in Sacramento. Diwali is also known as the Festival of Lights and is the most widely celebrated festival in India.

It signifies the triumph of good over evil celebrated by Hindu, Jain, and Sikh faiths. This was the third time in its history that Diwali was celebrated at the California State Capitol. BAPS organized this event by partnering with Assemblymember Ash Kalra, Assemblymember Alex Lee, Assemblymember Jasmeet Bains and Senator Dave Cortese.

The Chief Clerk of the California State Assembly Sue Parker was also in attendance. The festival was celebrated with an annakut, an offering of traditional, vegetarian dishes to the sacred images of God. The event was a unifying opportunity to celebrate Diwali in the state's capitol, where attendees had the chance to reflect on the universal messages of Diwali, while also increasing awareness about the Hindu & Indian American community and interfaith harmony.

Additionally, attendees had valuable interactions enhancing the event's impact and significance.

options.headline: HH Pramukh Swami Maharaj's Asthipushpa Visarjan, Bharuch, India
options.story:
The Vedic ceremony to scatter the sacred ashes of Brahmaswarup Pramukh Swami Maharaj in the holy River Narmada was performed by Pragat Brahmaswarup Mahant Swami Maharaj, sadguru sadhus and dignitaries in the presence of 8,000 devotees. Especially present on this auspicious occasion were three former ministers of the Narmada project – Shri Bhupendrasinh Chudasma, Shri Jaynarayanbhai Vyas and Shri Siddharthbhai Patel.

The River Narmada is regarded as the lifeline of Gujarat as it provides water to many parts of the state. The initial mahapuja rituals commenced at 3.45 p.m. in the grounds of Narmada Park where the devotees were seated. At 4.45 p.m., HH Mahant Swami Maharaj arrived at the banks of the river where a decorative platform had been created using barges.

Mahant Swami Maharaj performed the concluding rituals and then scattered the asthipushpa (sacred ashes) of Brahmaswarup Pramukh Swami Maharaj into the holy River Narmada. The former ministers, other dignitaries, senior devotees and sadhus from various BAPS mandirs then also scattered Brahmaswarup Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s sacred ashes into the holy river.

Thereafter, an assembly in the adjacent Narmada Park was held based on the theme ‘Pramukh Swami Maharaj – Our Lifeline’, depicting the various ways by which Pramukh Swami Maharaj nurtured the spiritual and social lives of individuals and society. The program featured speeches by senior sadhus and the three former ministers, as well as video shows.

The assembly concluded with the blessings of HH Mahant Swami Maharaj.
